newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Oops, Swiss army embarrassed again by latest drill.
newsitem.headline: Oops, Swiss army embarrassed again by latest drill.

text.p: Outraged farmers and railway officials demanded the Swiss government rein in the army on Friday after red-faced military brass acknowledged soldiers had practised subduing unruly farmers and striking rail workers.

The revelation of last week's drill was the latest embarrassment for the army, which a week ago owned up to staging a manoeuvre in which tanks warded off a hypothetical invasion from neighbouring Italy's secessionist Padania movement.

The president of the Swiss Farmers Association, the Swiss Federal Railways chief and the vice president of the Railway Workers Association issued a joint statement decrying the drill and urging the governmment to ban such "military games".
Defence Ministry spokesman Martin Buehler said the exercise by reserve soldiers doing two weeks of active duty was "completely off the mark".

It violated instructions the army chief of staff issued in September that military exercises could not be based on real events touching on domestic or foreign policy, he said, adding the officer who planned the drill was being questionned.
The ministry has been sensitive to controversy since another army unit in June drilled by pretending to help police break up a riot by jobless Swiss.

Switzerland's militia-style army holds frequent manoeuvres to keep its draftee force trim for defending the neutral state, although it has not fought a battle since losing to a French army in 1515 at Marignano -- in what is now Italy.
The last time its soldiers opened fire was to mow down striking workers in Geneva in 1932, killing 13.
